pending_diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS: Severe Ergotism (Vasospastic Limb Ischemia) secondary to drug-drug interaction THE SMOKING GUN: Co-administration of Clarithromycin (a potent CYP3A4 inhibitor) with Ergotamine Tartrate PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: Ergotamine relies heavily on hepatic clearance via the cytochrome P450 3A4 (CYP3A4) enzyme system. Potent CYP3A4 inhibitors, such as macrolide antibiotics (clarithromycin), block ergotamine metabolism, causing toxic serum accumulation. Elevated ergotamine levels induce prolonged stimulation of vascular alpha-adrenergic and 5-HT1B/1D serotonin receptors, resulting in severe, sustained peripheral arterial vasospasm, tissue hypoxia, metabolic acidosis, and potential gangrene if uncorrected.
